source: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM — GA_Statewide_2018_B18_DRRA (lidar, flown 2018, published 2022-05-31)
derivedVia: 3DEPElevation ImageServer exportImage, F32, resampled to the NAIP frame
license: public domain (US federal work) — redistributable, same class as NAIP
render: multi-directional hillshade, 4 azimuths (315/45/135/225) at 28-35 deg altitude, p1-p99 contrast stretch, gamma 0.9
why: lidar is an ACTIVE sensor: no sun, therefore no shadows. This shows the terrain breaks the 2022-01-10 optical basemap loses in shadow.
notALimitationOf: resolution — source posting is 1 m, coarser than NAIP's 0.6 m. This is a shadow answer, not a sharpness answer.
registeredTo: IDENTICAL bounds to base-naip-2022-01-leafoff — drop-in layer, no re-registration

siblings.slope: lidar-slope-2018.png (0-30 deg ramp; a break of slope IS the border of several named areas)

coverageConfirmed: 2026-08-31, deterministically: TNM Access API returned exactly 1 one-metre DEM product covering the property bbox. One-metre DEM exists ONLY where lidar was flown, so its presence IS the coverage answer.
corroboration: Max elevation in frame 906.7 m; property.json records 902 m / 2959 ft at the house. Independent agreement.
